subject: Next steps: buying roadmap, security gatekeepers & procurement intro
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@corebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: buying roadmap, security gatekeepers & next steps

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few asks so we can align the next steps: 

What I took away (high level):
- Goal: pilot Redwood inference for fraud-detection feature in the core retail banking flow (Q3 target).
- Primary success criteria: sub-50ms median latency for inference at 50 rps, and evidence of data residency controls + audit logs.
- Budget: rough range discussed on call but still TBD at exec level.

Requests / asks:
1) Can you share an org chart or list of the folks who would be involved in the buying decision (economic buyer, engineering owner, security contact, legal/procurement)? A simple names + titles + emails list is perfect.
2) Who on your side owns vendor security questionnaires / SOC 2 evidence? If you can share their contact and any checklist we should expect, Diego will prepare a concise evidence pack.
3) Procurement / legal cadence: do you require an approved SOW before commercial review, or do you do parallel legal + commercial review?
4) Decision criteria: please share any non-negotiables (e.g., encryption keys, retention policy, SLA targets).

Next steps I propose:
- Diego will draft a one-pager on our security controls and a technical appendix for the pilot.
- I’ll prepare a draft SOW + procurement checklist and share that with your procurement contact once introduced.
- Schedule a 30-min alignment with security and procurement next week (if available).

I attached a short call recap (recap_call_notes.pdf). Please feel free to add or correct anything.

Thanks — I’ll hold a couple of time slots for a follow-up: Tue 5/18 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 5/19 09:00–11:00 PT. Which works best for you?

Best,
David Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: recap_call_notes.pdf (pdf)
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@corebank.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ethan Miller <ethan.miller@corebank.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: buying roadmap, security gatekeepers & next steps

Hi David —

Thanks for the clear summary — that matches my notes. Quick answers inline: 

1) Org contacts (high level):
   - Economic buyer: Laura Thompson, VP Product <laura.thompson@corebank.com>
   - Engineering owner: Ethan Miller, Dir Eng (platform) <ethan.miller@corebank.com>
   - Security: Aaron Patel, InfoSec Manager <aaron.patel@corebank.com>
   - Legal / Procurement: procure@corebank.com (team inbox) — primary rep is Mei Chen (mei.chen@corebank.com)

2) Security evidence: Aaron owns questionnaires and runs the vendor security review. He prefers a short security brief + attachments (SOC 2, architecture diagram, data flow). I can loop him in.

3) Procurement cadence: we typically do parallel legal and commercial review for pilots, but procurement will request an approved SOW for pilots >$50k. If you can share a draft SOW and a procurement checklist, Mei will confirm the exact docs they need.

4) Non-negotiables: 
   - Data must be stored in US-only regions for this pilot.
   - KMS integration or customer-managed keys preferred.
   - 30-day audit log retention minimum.

I’ll loop Aaron and Mei once you share the short security brief and the draft SOW. Wed 5/19 at 09:00 PT works well for Ethan and me.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Senior Product Manager | CoreBank

Thanks — copying Sofia so everyone stays in the loop. Quick tech/security notes for the brief: 

- I will produce a 1-page security summary with the following sections: network isolation & VPC options, KMS integrations (AWS KMS / customer-managed keys), data flow diagram, audit log/sample query, SOC 2 scope and recent report excerpt.
- For the pilot SLA: we'll confirm token-level latency targets but can propose a pilot SLO at 50ms median and 99th percentile at 250ms for the expected traffic shape.
- Suggested security questions to anticipate from Aaron/Mei:
   * Where are inference logs stored and for how long?
   * Can customer supply a KMS key or require Redwood-managed keys?
   * What is the data deletion workflow for model inputs?
   * Do we support private VPC deployments for the pilot?

I’ll attach the initial draft one-pager and a short appendix for the architecture in the next email.

Proposed next call: Wed 5/19 09:00 PT — I'll join and bring a short deck for security and deployment options.
